newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks storm to new record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks storm to new record.

text.p: The Mexican bourse shed some of its earlier advance on profit-taking, but still posted its second record close in a row on Thursday.

"You'd have to be crazy not to take profits like this. Today you could close your books up and still go home rich," a floor trader said. "It was mayhem all day. For most of it we just couldn't sell enough," her added.
The blue chip IPC share index ended up 93.60 points, or 1.88 percent, at a record 5,067.87. Earlier, the IPC barely paused on its way to 5,127.70 as bullish investors rushed into Mexico.

Analysts said stocks gained international funds on the run from Asia and the U.S. bond market had settled on Mexico in the wake of landmark mid-term elections on July 6, which investors gave a clean bill of health.

"People don't want to miss the party...There is portfolio reallocation within dedicated Latam funds and people are reassessing Brazil risk," Todd Edwards, Latin American equity staregist at the Latinvest brokerage.
For Geoffrey Dennis, emerging markets equity strategist at HSBC-James Capel, liquidity was "driving fundamental valuation."
"An extra positive was a warm reception to the elections," he added.
The analysts noted U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yields had dipped to 6.30 percent, close to levels not seen since 1993, and released hefty liquidity into equity markets worldwide.

Vinod Seghal, equity research chief at the Societe General brokerage, noted the recent crop of earnings reports showed consumption was recovering in Mexico after being in the doldrums since the 1994 devaluation crisis.
"Kimber is a catch-up story and banks are the ultimate consumer story," he said.

Paper company Kimberly Clark de Mexico (Kimber) -- in which Kimberly Clark Corp has a minority stake -- gained 1.60 pesos to 37.00 pesos. The stock mirrored the broad market by ending off a high of 38.10 pesos.
Banacci, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, ended up 1.20 pesos at 23.00 pesos, but had earlier risen so high the bourse imposed a trading halt.

Seghal also noted that conglomerate Grupo Carso continued to post record gains in the wake of news the company showed signs of turning around its recent acquisition, troubled retailer Sears de Mexico.
"The timing of the Sears buy looks to have been very good, Carso could be a bellwether again," he said.
On the broad market, gains outstripped slides 82 to 39 with a high total of 134 stocks traded.
Trading volume and turnover were exceedingly heavy at 248.9 million shares and 3.88 billion pesos ($496.7 million), respectively.
